installer_meta.maintainer_note: Community-maintained (exotic edition). The installer asks for the init system (installer_meta.init_systems, OpenRC first as the default): installer_meta.init_packages names the init and its elogind provider for basestrap/pacstrap, because base alone lets pacman pick dinit's providers and a later openrc then conflicts with them; packages/*.json carry the per-init service packages (openssh-openrc, openssh-dinit, ...) and service names under init.<name>. basestrap is used on an Artix host; anywhere else — the FreedomNAS live ISO included — pacstrap does the same job from pacman, arch-install-scripts and artix-keyring (freedomnas-overlay), pointed at bootstrap_files.pacman_conf with a throwaway keyring and no host mirrorlist (-M). files.pacman_mirrorlist gives the installed system the same mirror. The kernel is linux-freedomnas with OpenZFS built in, from the FreedomNAS pacman repository (repositories.core), as on Arch: no DKMS, and files.freedomnas_uki_hook rebuilds the UKI on kernel updates because pacman never runs /etc/kernel/postinst.d. zfs-utils-freedomnas ships systemd units only; the service scripts zfs-openrc, zfs-dinit and zfs-runit come from the same repository, built by freedomnas-arch from codeberg.org/sarahmeow86/zfs-openrc and codeberg.org/sarahmeow86/zfs-dinit.

rootpool.create: zpool create {force} -o ashift={ashift} -O acltype=posixacl -O canmount=off -O compression={compression} -O dnodesize=auto -O normalization=formD -O relatime=on -O xattr=sa -O mountpoint=/ -R {altroot} {pool_name} {device}

pacman_conf.content:
[options]
Architecture = auto
SigLevel = Required DatabaseOptional
LocalFileSigLevel = Optional
GPGDir = {bootstrap_dir}/gnupg
ParallelDownloads = 5

[system]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirror2.artixlinux.org/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://artixlinux.mirror.garr.it/$repo/os/$arch

[world]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirror2.artixlinux.org/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://artixlinux.mirror.garr.it/$repo/os/$arch

[galaxy]
Server = {mirror}/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://mirror2.artixlinux.org/$repo/os/$arch
Server = https://artixlinux.mirror.garr.it/$repo/os/$arch

dracut_uki.content:
# The UKI is built inside a chroot, where dracut's idea of "this host" is
# the installer's, not the machine being installed.
hostonly="no"
# Wait for the root pool before importing it (assets/dracut/
# 91freedomnas-rootwait): a USB stick appears after the zfs module tries.
add_dracutmodules+=" freedomnas-rootwait freedomnas-fallback "
# dracut 111 (Arch/Artix) installs nothing for its "=drivers/<dir>" module
# lists, so an image booted from a USB stick has no usb-storage/uas to find
# its root pool and no USB keyboard in the rescue shell. Name the modules of
# those directories explicitly instead; dracut sets $kernel before reading
# this file.
add_drivers+=" $(find /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/usb/storage /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/usb/host /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/hid /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/input/keyboard /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/input/serio /lib/modules/$kernel/kernel/drivers/mmc -name '*.ko*' -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\.ko.*$//') "
# A NAS boots from its own disks, never over several paths to one LUN, and
# multipath-tools (pulled in by libvirt) brings a dracut module whose
# install step wants a systemd unit directory the other inits lack.
omit_dracutmodules+=" multipath "

fstab.content:
# /etc/fstab - ZFS datasets are mounted by ZFS, not fstab
{esp_spec}	/boot/efi	vfat	defaults	0	2

scheduled_jobs.content:
# FreedomNAS scheduled work. Cron decides when; config.yaml decides what,
# so a system with no policies costs a handful of no-ops a day.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
PYTHONPATH={install_root}/core
0  * * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval hourly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
5  0 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval daily   >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
10 0 * * 0  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval weekly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
15 0 1 * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval monthly >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
# The configuration's shadow copy on every other pool: what a reinstall
# onto a blank disk finds waiting for it on the data pool.
30 3 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas shadow-sync                     >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1

sudoers.content:
# FreedomNAS: the WebUI runs updates as the signed-in user,
# and topgrade calls sudo itself for the steps that need root.
%{sudo_group} ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

freedomnas_uki_hook.content:
# pacman never runs /etc/kernel/postinst.d, so the UKI is rebuilt here
# whenever a kernel is installed or upgraded.
[Trigger]
Type = Path
Operation = Install
Operation = Upgrade
Target = usr/lib/modules/*/vmlinuz

[Action]
Description = Rebuilding the FreedomNAS UKI...
When = PostTransaction
Exec = /bin/sh -c '[ -x /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki ] || exit 0; while read -r f; do /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki "$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")"; done'
NeedsTargets

freedomnas_uki_backup_hook.content:
# Before a kernel is installed or upgraded, the running UKI goes to the
# rollback slot (zz-dracut-uki --backup).
[Trigger]
Type = Path
Operation = Install
Operation = Upgrade
Target = usr/lib/modules/*/vmlinuz

[Action]
Description = Backing up the FreedomNAS UKI...
When = PreTransaction
Exec = /bin/sh -c '[ -x /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki ] || exit 0; /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki --backup'

samba_conf.content:
# Written by the FreedomNAS installer. Shares are created as usershares
# (net usershare) by the WebUI, so only the global settings live here.
[global]
   workgroup = WORKGROUP
   server string = FreedomNAS
   server role = standalone server
   security = user
   log file = /var/log/samba/%m.log
   max log size = 1000
   usershare path = /var/lib/samba/usershares
   usershare max shares = 100
   usershare allow guests = no

diagnostics.target_processes: [ {root} = / ] || for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ "$p/root" -ef /proc/1/root ] && continue; echo "${{p#/proc/}} root=$(readlink "$p/root" 2>/dev/null) $(tr '\0' ' ' < "$p/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)"; done
